name: Old Canberra Brickworks (Yarralumla Brickworks)
area: Yarralumla — Section 102, Block 1; public-road vicinity via Denman Street
status: Disused historic industrial site — access not confirmed; permission required
notes: Historic brickworks established in 1913, production began in 1916 and ceased in 1976. ACT heritage-listed. An ACT Government transport report describes the site as not in operation and notes access was provided off Denman Street; this is not permission to enter and the site may be redeveloped or restricted. View only from public roads unless the land manager confirms lawful public access. No precise pin supplied because visitor access is not confirmed. Checked 12 Nov 2026. Sources: https://www.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0009/1945872/canberra-brickworks-precinct-conservation-management-plan-2021-volume-1.pdf ; https://www.legislation.act.gov.au/DownloadFile/di/2021-195/current/PDF/2021-195.PDF ; https://dafinder.blob.core.windows.net/dadocuments/DOCs/TRAFFICREPORT-202342069-01.pdf

name: Callam Offices (Former Woden TAFE Complex)
area: Callam Street, Phillip ACT 2606 — public street frontage only; use public footpaths.
status: Closed / vacant government office and education complex — redevelopment plans under consideration
notes: Distinctive three-pod, space-age office complex built between 1977 and 1981 and later used by Woden TAFE. The buildings have been empty since mid-2025. In September 2026, reporting on an ACT Legislative Assembly hearing said the Government was considering selling the site and that major refurbishment would be costly. This is a street-view research stop only: do not enter the buildings or grounds, which may be unsafe or restricted. Confirm current redevelopment status before visiting. Source: https://region.com.au/government-wants-to-offload-heritage-listed-woden-landmark-eyes-adaptive-reuse/996239/

name: 91A Wakefield Gardens — Vacant Government Building
area: 91A Wakefield Gardens, Ainslie ACT 2602 — view from the public street only.
status: Long-term vacant government building — not fit for occupation
notes: An obscure former government property reported vacant for more than 20 years. An ACT Government answer to a 2025 Estimates question said the building was not fit for occupation because of hazardous materials including asbestos and lead paint, and that a future use was being assessed. The building itself was described as being in very poor condition and unlikely to be reusable. Do not enter or approach the structure; view only from public space. Source: https://www.parliament.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0009/2902266/QON-215-Answer-iCBR-Planning-Property-at-Wakefield-Gardens-LEE.pdf

name: Former CSIRO Forestry Site
area: Former CSIRO campus, Yarralumla ACT — use public roads only; some buildings may still be occupied.
status: Former research campus — largely vacated, some private offices remain
notes: A lesser-known former research and forestry campus. The CSIRO vacated the Yarralumla site in 2022 as it consolidated facilities in Canberra, although the National Capital Authority says small private-sector offices continue to occupy some buildings. Included as a former-use / changing-site lead, not a confirmed fully abandoned location. Do not enter buildings or private grounds. Source: https://www.nca.gov.au/planning/public-consultations/national-capital-plan-draft-amendment-97-block-7-section-4-yarralumla

name: Former Kaleen Indoor Sports Centre
area: 16 Georgina Crescent, Kaleen ACT 2617 — former site; view only from public roads
status: Closed 2 October 2026 — former indoor sports facility; redevelopment / demolition planned
notes: Former Kaleen Indoor Sports Centre, also known as Kaleen Indoor Recreation Centre. The historic address is 16 Georgina Crescent, Kaleen ACT 2617. The centre closed on 2 October 2026 and the site owner planned demolition and redevelopment with residential buildings and a smaller indoor sports facility. This is a former-site entry for local history and mapping only; do not enter the property or any demolition / construction area. View only from public space. Sources: https://region.com.au/petitions-couldnt-save-kaleen-indoor-sports-centre-now-it-prepares-for-demolition/1000010/ ; https://www.sport.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0017/811331/ACT-Indoor-Facilities-Combined-Document.pdf Map pin uses the published address coordinates; pin marks the former site, not an invitation to enter.
